name: Building systems (conveying, fire protection, low voltage, security)

items.name: Hydraulic passenger elevator, low-rise (2–4 stops), installed

cost.method: e1 commercial hydraulic $75,000–$150,000 turnkey low-rise. Low = $75k; mid = $115k ≈ midpoint of e1 (rounded up for 3–4 stops); high = $160k, slightly above e1 to cover 4-stop / 3,500 lb cars. Single low-confidence cost-guide source — verify with an elevator contractor quote.

items.notes: Per car incl. cab, jack, power unit, controller, door equipment and installation. Excludes the hoistway, pit and machine room construction (in shell) and power feeder. MRL traction is a common alternative at similar cost.

items.name: Traction passenger elevator, mid-rise (≈5–10 stops), installed

cost.method: e1 traction $150,000–$350,000+ (mid- and higher-rise). Low = $150k; mid = $250k = midpoint of e1; high = $400k reflecting the '+' and e2's $50k–$100k per landing at ~5+ landings for office/retail. High-rise (15+ stops, 500+ fpm) exceeds the high — add per stop.

items.notes: Per car, geared/gearless or MRL. Excludes hoistway construction and power feeders.

items.name: Automatic fire sprinkler system, new construction (per SF of sprinklered area)

cost.method: e3 straightforward new construction wet-pipe $1.50–$3/SF; e4 dry-pipe $4–$9/SF where dry equipment and layout changes are needed. Low = $1.75 (large open wet-pipe buildings), mid = $3.00 (top of e3, allowing riser/backflow/FDC in small-to-mid buildings), high = $5.00 (partial dry/pre-action, low end of e4). Excludes fire pump and water service.

items.notes: NFPA 13/13R wet system incl. riser, backflow preventer and FDC. Fire pump (if required) and site fire line are separate. Retrofit in occupied buildings runs $4–$12/SF per the same source.

items.name: Addressable fire alarm / detection system, new construction (per SF)

cost.method: e5 standard installation $1–$5/SF (retrofits $4–$12+). New construction sits in the lower part of e5: low = $1 (warehouse/simple occupancies), mid = $2, high = $4 (residential/hotel with in-unit devices, voice evac). Single low-confidence source.

items.notes: FACP, initiating and notification devices, wiring, programming and testing. Mass notification / high-rise voice evac and elevator recall interfaces push to the high end.

items.name: Structured cabling (Cat6 horizontal + backbone, IDF/MDF racks) per SF

cost.method: Derived from per-drop cost. e6 Cat6 drop $125–$250 installed (2025). Office density ≈ 1 drop per 75–100 SF (≈2 drops per workstation at 150–200 SF/person, judgment) → $1.25–$3.33/SF; add ≈20% for backbone fiber, racks, patch panels and testing → ≈$1.50–$4.00. Low $1.25 for low-density uses (retail/warehouse office areas), mid $2.50, high $4.00 (dense office, Cat6A). 2025 evidence expressed in 2026 dollars (gap ≤1 yr).

items.notes: Tenant/owner data cabling only. Excludes active network equipment, Wi-Fi APs, DAS/ERRCS and AV.

items.name: Card access control, per controlled door (reader, lock/strike, controller share, install)

cost.method: e7 all-in first-year cost $1,500–$4,500 per door incl. hardware, setup, software and configuration (installation alone $500–$2,000). Low/high = e7; mid = $2,800 ≈ midpoint, rounded down slightly because multi-door systems share panels/software.

items.notes: Interior doors toward low, exterior/high-security toward high. Biometric readers and turnstiles are extra.

items.name: IP video surveillance camera, installed (incl. cabling and share of NVR/VMS)

cost.method: Derived (no camera-specific source fetched). Commercial IP camera $300–$1,200 hardware (judgment) + one Cat6 drop $125–$250 (e6, used as proxy for the camera run, often longer than an office drop) + mounting/labor $300–$800 + allocated NVR/VMS license/storage $200–$700 ≈ $1,000–$3,000 per camera, mid $1,800. Multi-sensor/PTZ cameras exceed the high.

items.notes: Per camera position. Pole-mounted parking lot cameras need poles and conduit (site work) on top.

source.title: How Much Does Elevator Installation Cost?

evidence.quote: Commercial hydraulic elevators commonly fall around $75,000 to $150,000 … traction elevators reaching roughly $150,000 to $350,000+.
evidence.scopeNotes: Consumer/business cost guide (updated Aug 26, 2026); turnkey per elevator; hydraulic = low-rise, traction = mid/high-rise. low/high span both types.

source.title: How Much Does Elevator Installation Cost?

evidence.quote: Day Elevator estimates roughly $50,000 to $100,000 per landing
evidence.scopeNotes: Per landing (stop), office and retail projects; secondary citation of an elevator contractor.

source.title: How Much Does a Commercial Fire Sprinkler System Cost?

evidence.quote: A commercial fire sprinkler system costs about $1.50 to $3 per square foot in straightforward new construction.
evidence.scopeNotes: Wet-pipe, new construction; page notes permits, water service and pumps may be excluded.

source.title: How Much Does a Commercial Fire Sprinkler System Cost?

evidence.quote: could rise to $4 to $9 per square foot when dry-pipe equipment and layout changes are needed
evidence.scopeNotes: Dry-pipe systems; same page gives retrofits at $4–$12/SF and pre-action $6–$15/SF.

source.title: How Much Does a Commercial Fire Alarm System Cost?

evidence.quote: generally costs about $1 to $5 per square foot for a standard installation
evidence.scopeNotes: Commercial fire alarm, standard installation (updated Aug 30, 2026); difficult retrofits $4–$12+/SF.

source.title: How much does it cost to install CAT-6 cabling?

evidence.quote: The average price per data drop for CAT-6 cabling is $125 to $250, including materials and labor.
evidence.scopeNotes: Per drop, materials + labor; consumer-oriented, not commercial-specific (updated Jan 31, 2025).

source.title: Key Card Door Lock System Price: Overview & Guide (2026)

evidence.quote: typically run $1,500–$4,500 per door, including hardware, setup, software licensing, and configuration
evidence.scopeNotes: Integrator blog (updated Mar 26, 2026); first-year all-in per door. Installation alone quoted at $500–$2,000 per door.
